title: Smudging, sage, and clearing a space
answer: Smudging is the practice of burning an herb, often white sage or another traditional plant, and moving the smoke through a room or around yourself as a way of clearing. People use it when a space feels heavy, after an argument, or when they move. It is a ritual, not a disinfectant and not a medical treatment. The shop sells sage and related incense when it is in stock. The guide Smudging: How to Clean and Clear Yourself and a Space is the short how-to. Her longer essay is Cleansing Rituals, Smudging. That essay is under Library, then Articles. Do not read a website address.

title: Amethyst
answer: Amethyst is a violet variety of quartz. Iron and natural irradiation make the purple. The Greek name means not drunken. It shows up from pale lilac to deep grape, depending on where it grew. People have traditionally reached for it when they want a clear head, quiet, or help with intuition, and it is often paired with the crown. That is tradition. It is also just a beautiful mineral. Her essay calls it the Swiss Army knife because people use it for so many ordinary intentions. That essay is under Library, then Articles. Do not read a website address.
